description:
Get which company the workspace itself is: the confirmed own-company anchor (`anchor`) and any detected companies not yet confirmed as it (`candidates`).

Use this whenever a question turns on "mine" versus "theirs" — my payables, my receivables, invoices I owe, what we billed — and then filter by the `company_id` this returns. Never decide which records are the workspace's own by comparing a company NAME: the same legal entity appears under several labels (a registered name, a trade name, a bank-issued label), so a name filter silently drops rows.

Returns `anchor` (`company_id`, `registered_name`, `trade_name`) or null when the workspace has not resolved one yet, and `candidates` (each with `company_id`, names, `role`, `confidence_score`, `state`). `own_identity` reports the identity detector's last verdict for the workspace (`decision`, `reason`, `pending`, `suggestions`) — detection output, never a confirmed anchor.

`anchor: null` means the workspace has no confirmed own company. Say so plainly and do not promote a candidate to the anchor yourself — a candidate is a detection, not a decision, and confirming one is a user action.

`own_companies` lists the companies the workspace counts as itself, each with its `basis`; it is the whole set only when `own_companies_complete` is true. When `own_companies_complete` is false the list is cut: a company missing from it may still be the workspace's own, so do not treat any company as "theirs" on the strength of this list alone, and say the own set is incomplete. `anchor` and `holder` rows are the workspace's own by proof; a `holder` row (the company behind a connected account) is the workspace's own even while `anchor` is null, so name it and say the anchor is not confirmed yet. `self_candidate` is a detection, not proof: mention it as possible only. For any mine-versus-theirs filter use the `company_id` of every `anchor` and `holder` row, never `anchor` alone.

⚠️ TO ASK THE USER WHICH COMPANY on a card so they can pick or search for it, call `well_show_company_candidates` INSTEAD: it draws a tile per candidate with a registry search and waits for the click. This read draws nothing.

Registry tax ids and registered addresses are deliberately not returned.

Call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. Both the anchor and the candidates are read from the same workspace this call is scoped to.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. This read reports one workspace's own data. Omit it and the token's primary workspace answers, which may not be the one you mean; the result names the workspace that did.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_get_own_company

registry_country.description: The own company's registry country as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, null when unknown.

adoption_preview_counts.description: How much of the company's history confirming it would bring in, per kind: documents, tasks, transactions and accounts. capped true means the count stopped at its ceiling, so say more than that number. Null when it is not known yet (no tax id on the candidate, or the preview was skipped).

business_type.description: The company's legal form (SAS, Inc, GmbH), when known.

candidate_id.description: The candidate's id — pass to well_create_company_workspace to mint the company workspace from it.

confirmable.description: Whether well_create_company_workspace accepts this candidate now. False for a name-only detected candidate with no groundable identity, or one that has left the surfaced set.

confirmable_reason.description: Why confirmable is false, null when true. not_grounded: no registry or tax identifier to mint from; ask the user to search the registry and pick the verified entry. not_open: no longer the surfaced candidate; re-read the own-company list before acting. Others: not_primary, already_confirmed, not_surfaceable.

country.description: The company's country, for a light detail panel.

domain.description: The company's domain, a logo source and a display fallback.

existing_workspace_id.description: An existing workspace the person manages whose company matches this candidate, offered to attach instead of minting a duplicate. Null on every row the offer classifier did not clear.

existing_workspace_relation.description: How the offered workspace relates to this one. child: it is already an active child. top_level: attaching links it under this workspace. Null whenever existing_workspace_id is.

remote_logo_url.description: A resolved logo url when one is known; null otherwise.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

own_companies.description: The companies the workspace counts as itself, anchor first, then holders, then self-candidates. Filter mine-versus-theirs by the company_id of every anchor and holder row, never by anchor alone. Empty when the workspace has none.

basis.description: Why the workspace counts this company as itself. anchor: the confirmed own company. holder: the company that holds a connected account; proven, even while anchor is null. self_candidate: a detection, not proof; mention it as possible only.

own_companies_complete.description: True when own_companies is the whole own set. False when it was cut at a bound: a company missing from it may still be the workspace's own, so never classify a company as theirs from this list.

ask_kind.description: When decision is ask, what is being asked: companies_or_clients (pick the real own company among several), conflicting_anchor_identity (evidence disagrees with the anchor), pending_identifier (a named company lacks a legal identifier), confirm_entity (one named company is proposed; confirm it is the user's own).

company_id.description: The company the verdict proposes or anchors on, when one was named.

company_ids.description: Public ids of every company subject the verdict surfaced — the proposal and ask subjects.

decision.description: The own-identity detector's last completed verdict for this workspace — propose (a company worth proposing), ask (ambiguity a person must resolve), or none. Null when no detection pass has settled yet.

holder_candidates.description: Registry entries a lookup found for bank holders the detector judged to be organisations, normally none or one. A lead for the user's registry pick, not a confirmed identity and not a proposal: it names no workspace company, decision can stay none beside it, and its identifier is withheld.

scheme.description: The kind of identifier the entry is known by, never its value.

pending.description: True while an identity-resolution pass is queued or in flight — a fresher decision may follow; re-read after it settles.

reason.description: The audit reason the verdict carries, in the resolver-reason vocabulary.

registry_candidates.description: For an ask whose companies lack a legal identifier: the one registry entry a lookup found for a company, when exactly one matched. A lead for the user's registry pick, not a confirmed identity; its identifier is withheld.

company_id.description: The company a registry entry was found for.

scheme.description: The kind of identifier the entry is known by, never its value.

suggestions.description: Ranked suggestions the detector folded — leads, not proposal cards; a person's pick is what admits one.

own_identity.description: The own-identity module's decision for this workspace, or null when the workspace row could not be read. A decision is a detection output, never a confirmed anchor — only anchor is confirmed.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

title: Get own company
